interpretation: Three G-codes (G0556, G0557, G0558) billed once per calendar month, after an initiating visit where required, by the physician or NP, PA, CNM or CNS who intends to be responsible for the patient's primary care and the continuing focal point for all needed services. No specialty restriction.
No minimum time per month and no time-based billing restrictions. Not every service element must be furnished in every billed month; elements are furnished as medically necessary.

Patient with one or fewer chronic conditions expected to last at least 12 months or until death that place the patient at significant risk of death, acute exacerbation or decompensation, or functional decline.
Patient with two or more such chronic conditions.

Patient who is a Qualified Medicare Beneficiary with two or more such chronic conditions. CMS notes practitioners can see QMB status when verifying Medicare eligibility, and providers may not bill QMBs for Medicare cost sharing.
Patient consent obtained at initiation and documented in the medical record; verbal consent is sufficient. New consent is required if the billing practitioner changes.

Required for new patients. Not required for established patients: seen by the practitioner or the same practice in the past 3 years, or received APCM, CCM (99487, 99489, 99490, 99491, 99439, 99437) or PCM (99424 to 99427) from the practice in the past year. A Medicare AWV by the APCM practitioner can serve as the initiating visit.

Reasonable after-hours access for urgent needs; real-time access to the medical record is not required, but the after-hours responder must document and communicate the interaction to the primary care team.
Patient-centered comprehensive care plan element finalized as proposed.
Reasonable efforts at timely follow-up within 7 days of an ED visit or hospital discharge when possible, with efforts and contacts documented.
Practitioner, home- and community-based care coordination and enhanced communication (secure messaging, portal, other communication technology-based services) finalized as proposed.
Practice uses data to manage preventive and chronic care across its patient population; finalized as proposed.

MIPS eligible clinicians must register for and report the Value in Primary Care MVP. Shared Savings Program ACO, ACO REACH, Primary Care First and Making Care Primary participants meet the requirement through those programs; it does not apply to clinicians who are not MIPS eligible.

CCM, PCM, TCM, interprofessional consultation, remote evaluation of patient images or video, virtual check-ins and e-visits (Table 26) may not be billed for the patient in the same month by the practitioner who bills APCM. Other practitioners, including in the same practice, may bill them when medically necessary.
